title: Diffusion bridge with randomized initial and terminal times and its application to fish migration
summary: We mathematically model the dynamics of the number of migratory fish observed at a fixed location along a river in a random environment. Particularly, as a new approach, we construct a stochastic differential equation that incorporates the influence of environmental factors on the fluctuations in the start and end of migration. The model is a diffusion bridge with a non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, called the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross bridge, and has random initial and terminal times arising from time-change, so that the influences of environmental factors can be efficiently incorporated.
